questions_and_answers.question_text: How can an Italian statement be turned into a question?

answers.answer_text: By adding no? or vero? to it
By adding non at the beginning
By changing the verb to the future tense

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which expression means 'Pleased to meet you'?

answers.answer_text: Lei è la signora Contini, vero?
Lavoro in questa sezione da quattro anni.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which verb is primarily used for knowing or being acquainted with people or places?
What does a present verb form used with da plus a period of time indicate?

answers.answer_text: How long something has been going on
What will happen in the future
What happened only once in the past

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the normal situation with possessives in Italian?

answers.answer_text: They are expressed with the definite article

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the future form of io essere given in the text?
Which preposition connects certain nouns or adjectives to a following infinitive in the examples given?
What does the capitalized La attached to an infinitive stand for?

answers.answer_text: A formal singular direct object you
A definite article for masculine nouns

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which day of the week is feminine?

articles.text:
Language -Usage Notes
1. Any statement may be turned into a question byadding no? or vero? to it.
Thus:
Lei è la signora Contini, no?
You are Mrs. Contini, aren 't you?
Lei è la signora Contini, vero?
You are Mrs. Contini, aren 't you?
2. The expressions commonly used in introductions are:
Piacere.
Molto piacere.
Piacere di conoscerla. How do you do?
(or)
Pleased to meet you.
3. You have had two verbs for to know--conoscere and sapere. The former
is primari/y used to express the idea of knowing or being acquainted with
people or places. The latter is used for most other kinds of knowing.
sapere ---------..~ So tutto. I know everything.
4. A present verb form used with da (+ period of time) refers to how long
something has been going ono Thus, note the translations:

5. You have had several examples of p ossessi ves (for my or your) being
expressed with the definite article (il, la, i, etc.). This is the normal situation
with p ossessi ves in Italian. Exceptions ta this rule are to be learned as they
o ccu r. Here are the four forms of mio (my) and Suo (your), together
with their definite articles. Notice the irregular masculine plural forms.

le mie valigie

6. Notice the future farms sarò (1 will be) and sarà (you, she, he, it will be,)
as well as mi troverò (1 will find myself.). Future farms af these verbs are:
(io) sarò mi troverò
(lei) sarà si troverà
{noi} saremo ci troveremo
(voi) sarete vi troverete

7. Certa in nouns or adjectives are connected to a following infinitive by a
preposition. You have two examples of this in the dia/og.
piacere di conoscerla
lieta di aiutarla
8. Note the capitalized La attached to the infinitive less fina/ -e (conoscerla,
aiutarLa--compare arrivederla). The form la stands for a formaI singular
direct object you.
9. Normally the word sempre immediate/y follows a verb. With the past time
phrase, it may a/so come between the two parts of the phrase. Thus:
10. Ha lavorato sempre in questa sezione?
(or)
Ha sempre lavorato in questa sezione?
The days of the week are:
lunedì Monday
martedì Tuesday
mercoledì Wednesday
giovedì Thursday
venerdì Friday
sabato Saturday
domenica Sunday
They are ali masculine except fordomenica, which is feminine.
